title: What If a Country Stopped Making Pennies? Canada Did

scenes.text: What if a country simply stopped making pennies? Canada did, in 2013.
Each penny cost the government about 1.6 cents to make, so every single one lost money.
On February 4, 2013, the Royal Canadian Mint stopped distributing them. Old pennies stayed legal to spend.
Cash totals were rounded to the nearest five cents, so a shop never needed a penny in change.
Card payments and cheques were not rounded at all, so those totals stayed exact.
The change was expected to save taxpayers about 11 million dollars a year.

description:
What if a country stopped making pennies?
Canada ended distribution on February 4, 2013, because each coin cost about 1.6 cents to produce.
